overview: Lendlease Group is a Sydney-headquartered, ASX-listed diversified real estate group structured as a stapled security (Lendlease Corporation Limited shares stapled to Lendlease Trust units). It operates through three core segments - Investments (international real estate funds/asset management plus a co-investment portfolio), Development (large-scale mixed-use precincts, build-to-rent and build-to-sell residential, workplace) and Construction (project delivery for government and corporate clients, now Australia-only) - with a transitional Capital Release Unit (CRU) winding down legacy international and non-core assets. Since a May 2024 strategy reset, the Group has been divesting its international construction and non-core offshore development assets to reweight capital toward a higher-returning, more capital-efficient, Australia-focused Investments-led model.

business_model.summary: Lendlease earns recurring funds/asset management fees and co-investment income from its Investments platform, project-based development profit from converting land/entitlements into completed real estate (often seeded into its own funds, i.e. 'develop-to-core'), and construction fees/margins from delivering projects for government and corporate clients. A separate CRU segment is a temporary, non-guided vehicle recycling capital out of legacy international and non-core assets; it is not a continuing revenue stream and is expected to shrink to nothing as divestments complete.

revenue_streams.name: Investments (funds/asset mgmt fees, co-investment income, transaction & performance fees)
revenue_streams.trend: structurally targeted to grow to ~50% of long-run IDC EBITDA mix, but FUM and management fees declined in FY26 amid portfolio recycling

revenue_streams.name: Construction (fee-based & fixed-price project delivery, Australia only)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - revenue +29% YoY to $3.9b in FY26, margin recovered to 4.3% EBITDA margin, backlog +42% to $8.4b

revenue_streams.name: Development (development profit on project completion/sale)
revenue_streams.trend: depressed in FY26 on low completions; expected to recover FY27-FY28 as One Circular Quay, Victoria Harbour, One Darling Point and Comcentre complete

revenue_streams.name: Capital Release Unit (legacy/non-core asset divestment - transitional, not guided)
revenue_streams.trend: winding down - $(500)m EBITDA loss in FY26 from impairments; $3.4b of recycling contracted/completed to date, more targeted for FY27

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B institutional (sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, superannuation funds as capital partners; governments and corporates as construction/development clients) and B2C (build-to-rent residents, apartment buyers, retail/workplace tenants)
business_model.geographic_mix: Historically global, now re-weighting sharply to Australia (target >75% of invested capital in Australia 'over time'; FUM currently ~63% Australia / 37% offshore across Asia, UK and US); international construction (US and UK) fully divested in FY26

main_competitors: large Australian contractors (CPB Contractors/CIMIC, Multiplex, Built, Hutchinson Builders)
competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest Australian-listed real estate funds management platform by scale behind Charter Hall (per industry commentary), with a historically unusual integrated model spanning funds management, development and construction; now retrenching from a global development/investment footprint to an Australia-centric, capital-light 'Investments-led' strategy

moat_factors.description: Ability to originate and develop projects, then seed them into its own managed funds, gives a differentiated, capital-efficient pipeline for growing funds under management (FUM) that pure-play managers lack

moat_factors.factor: Tier-1 Australian construction reputation & government relationships
moat_factors.description: Decades of delivery on defence, health, social infrastructure and metro rail projects drives a high proportion of repeat business and preferred-partner status ($5.2b of preferred work at FY26)
Track record on large precincts (Barangaroo, Melbourne Quarter, One Sydney Harbour) differentiates it in competitions for complex, large-scale mixed-use sites

moat_factors.factor: Scale of global funds/asset management platform
moat_factors.description: 36 funds and mandates across Australia and Asia and $43.9b of FUM, but FUM has been shrinking (from $48.9b a year earlier) amid recycling and outflows rather than growing

weaknesses: No durable economic moat per independent analysts (e.g. Morningstar) - operates in highly competitive, capital-intensive, cyclical development, funds management and construction markets
Multi-year track record of execution misses, write-downs and impairments (international construction, MSG North, Communities land, Forum and Keyton Trust)
Elevated financial leverage (reported gearing 30.3% vs a 5-15% through-cycle target) constrains flexibility and has already produced a credit profile near the bottom of investment grade
Shrinking FUM base erodes the recurring fee income the new 'Investments-led' strategy is meant to be built on
Repeated slippage of self-set targets - the 15% underlying gearing target originally set for end-FY26 was missed and pushed into FY27

growth_drivers: Completion of the Capital Release Unit wind-down and international construction/non-core asset exit, targeted to materially reduce gearing and free capital for growth in FY27

Impact Partnership Joint Venture with The Crown Estate (announced/commenced post FY26 balance date) - targeted to create up to $24b of new investment product (build-to-rent, life sciences, innovation, sustainable office) over the next decade
Growing Australian development pipeline, which closed FY26 at $13.2b (up from $9.8b), including residential, build-to-rent, workplace and emerging data centre/logistics opportunities
Record Australian Construction backlog ($8.4b, +42% YoY) plus $5.2b of preferred work in defence, social infrastructure, transport and data centres
New external Group CEO (Nick O'Neil, effective 24 August 2026) bringing capital-markets and real-asset management experience to drive the next phase of capital discipline and growth
Secular tailwinds in Australian real estate: housing undersupply, government infrastructure/defence/data-centre spending, and the institutionalisation of build-to-rent as an asset class

Capital partnering model (joint ventures, structured land payments) that lets Lendlease bring in third-party capital early, reducing balance-sheet intensity while still capturing development and funds management fees

business.description: Repeated delays and misses on self-set targets (CRU recycling, 15% gearing target slipped from FY26 to FY27) raise doubt about management's ability to deliver the May 2024 strategy on schedule

Large, long-dated development and legacy international assets have produced repeated impairments (MSG North, Communities land, Forum, Keyton Trust, retained international construction risk provisions) that drove a $(749)m FY26 statutory loss
FUM fell from $48.9b to $43.9b in FY26 on portfolio recycling and outflows, directly eroding the recurring management-fee base the Investments-led strategy depends on
Construction backlog is heavily weighted to a relatively small number of large government clients (defence, metro rail, hospitals), creating exposure to public capex cycles and contract timing

financial.description: Reported gearing of 30.3% (FY26) remains well above the 5-15% through-cycle target; net debt rose to $3.7b and interest cover fell to 2.5x from 3.6x
Ratings of Baa3 (Moody's, stable) and BBB- (Fitch, stable) sit at the lowest investment-grade notch; a further earnings shock could pressure a downgrade to sub-investment grade, raising funding costs

No Corporation dividend was declared in FY26 (reflecting the Group Operating Loss) and the full-year Trust distribution fell to 15.7 cents per security from 23.0 cents; further cuts are possible if OPAT stays weak
Remaining international assets (UK, US, Asia) and the new UK-focused Crown Estate joint venture still expose the Group to AUD/GBP/USD/SGD movements, even as the international footprint shrinks

regulatory.description: Large mixed-use precincts and rezonings (e.g. Rozelle Bay, Victorian Northern Freight precinct, South Brisbane riverfront) depend on lengthy, discretionary planning approval processes

Changes to CGT/negative gearing and other housing policy settings in Australia could alter the relative attractiveness of build-to-rent and institutional housing investment that underpins FUM growth plans

regulatory.risk: ESG, modern slavery and climate disclosure obligations
regulatory.description: Expanding mandatory climate-related financial disclosure and modern slavery reporting requirements across Australia and the UK increase compliance costs and scrutiny of the global supply chain

macro.description: Reported commentary of multiple 2026 RBA rate hikes directly raises funding costs (57% of debt is floating-rate) and pressures development feasibility and asset valuations; FY27 IDC guidance already reflects higher interest costs
Industry commentary expects cost escalation to remain above pre-2021 levels through 2027, squeezing development margins and fixed-price construction contracts

Development, construction and funds management are all highly cyclical and sensitive to GDP growth, population/migration trends and capital markets sentiment, directly affecting asset values, co-investment marks and transaction volumes

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Cautious recovery in Australian development and construction: housing undersupply and institutionalising build-to-rent demand are tailwinds, but elevated financing costs, construction cost inflation and feasibility constraints are tempering the pace of new starts; government infrastructure, defence and data-centre construction remain a bright spot
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - real estate development, funds management and construction are all closely tied to interest rates, GDP growth and capital markets conditions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - directly affects financing costs on a ~57% floating-rate debt book, development project feasibility, and valuations across the co-investment and funds management portfolios

recent_developments.event: Reported a statutory loss after tax of $(318)m (vs $48m profit pcp), driven by CRU valuation impairments and the announced MSG North land sale; IDC EPS guidance for FY26 maintained at 28-34 cents per security; interim distribution cut to 6.2 cents per security (Trust only, no Corporation dividend); shares fell to near four-decade lows

Announced $250m sale of MSG North land as part of continued CRU asset recycling; announced appointment of Nick O'Neil (Head of Australian Real Assets at AustralianSuper, ex-Macquarie) as new Group CEO and Managing Director, succeeding outgoing CEO Tony Lombardo (~2 decades at Lendlease); shares rallied ~4.6% on the appointment despite a reaffirmed FY26 loss outlook

Reported a statutory loss after tax of $(749)m (vs $225m profit in FY25), driven by non-cash CRU impairments/revaluations; IDC segment delivered OPAT of $233m and IDC EPS of 33.7 cents, at the top end of guidance; no final Corporation dividend and full-year Trust distribution cut to 15.7 cents per security (from 23.0 cents); shares fell roughly 6-11% depending on source; FY27 IDC EPS guidance set at 37-41 cents per security; Nick O'Neil's start date was brought forward from 10 September to 24 August 2026, with Andrew Nieland and Penny Ransom serving as Joint Interim CEOs in the interim

Commenced the Impact Partnership Joint Venture with The Crown Estate to accelerate master planning and land entitlement of a portfolio of UK development assets, targeted to create up to $24b of new investment product over the next decade

Issued $0.9b of perpetual subordinated hybrid securities in the Singapore and Australian dollar fixed income markets to support balance sheet liquidity and the equity-credit benefit used in reported gearing calculations

Board renewal continued: director David Craig retired (14 Nov 2025); Philip Coffey retired during FY26; Elizabeth Proust and Barbara Knoflach confirmed they will not seek re-election at the 2026 AGM; Philippa Kelly appointed as an independent Non-Executive Director (July 2026)
Credit ratings affirmed at Moody's Baa3 (stable, May 2026) and Fitch BBB- (stable, July 2026), both at the lowest investment-grade notch

items.vs_prior: raised (FY26 actual was 33.7 cents, itself at the top of the 28-34 cent FY26 guidance range)
items.notes: Supported by pre-sold apartment revenue in Development (One Circular Quay, Victoria Harbour) and continued Construction growth; partially offset by lower Investments co-investment and funds management income from portfolio recycling, the absence of large transactional profits, and higher interest costs
CRU remains a non-guided, transitional segment; focus is balancing value realisation against speed of execution as remaining ~$2.5b of invested capital (ex-contracted transactions) is recycled

items.period: Previously targeted end-FY26; now expected to be achieved via continued recycling into FY27
items.vs_prior: target missed/pushed out - proforma underlying gearing was 30.2% at FY26 year end
items.notes: Contingent on completion of ~$1b+ of further contracted/targeted CRU and IDC transactions and the receipt of related cash proceeds
No Corporation dividend was declared for FY26 given the Group Operating Loss; full-year Trust distribution was 15.7 cents per security

items.target: Investments ~50%, Development ~35%, Construction ~15% of IDC EBITDA
items.notes: FY26 actual mix was more heavily weighted to Investments (~55%) and Construction (~31%) with Development underweight (~14%) due to low completions
Group capital is still transitioning toward these targets as the CRU divests remaining international and non-core assets
Board has said a buyback will only occur once there is more certainty that underlying gearing will be sustainably at the 15% target and other pre-conditions are met

guidance.management_commentary: Joint Interim CEOs Andrew Nieland and Penny Ransom (pending Nick O'Neil's start) characterised FY26 as a transitional year and said FY27 is expected to be a stronger year for IDC earnings, underpinned by pre-sold Development revenue and continued Construction momentum, while flagging that Investments earnings will be impacted by lower co-investment and funds management income (from portfolio recycling) and higher interest costs, and that balance sheet strengthening via further CRU and IDC capital recycling remains the Group's top priority heading into FY27.

bull_case: The multi-year strategic reset (CRU wind-down, full exit of international construction, $3.4b+ of capital recycling completed/contracted to date) is nearing completion and should materially simplify and de-lever the Group by FY27

A newly appointed external CEO (Nick O'Neil, ex-AustralianSuper real assets head) was well received by the market and brings fresh capital-markets discipline to a business the Board itself describes as having completed its 'foundational' restructuring

FY27 IDC EPS guidance of 37-41 cents represents a step-up from FY26's 33.7 cents, supported by a replenished $13.2b Australian development pipeline and a record $8.4b Construction backlog plus $5.2b of preferred work

The Impact Partnership Joint Venture with The Crown Estate and continued capital partnering could add tens of billions of dollars of new investment product and FUM over the next decade at low balance-sheet cost

The stock trades at a steep discount to net tangible assets (NTA per security of $6.16 at FY26 year-end vs a depressed recent share price), suggesting potential re-rating if execution improves and asset sales complete near book value
bear_case: A long track record of execution misses and write-downs (international construction losses, MSG North, Communities land, Forum and Keyton Trust impairments) undermines confidence that the strategy will be delivered on the timelines management sets - the FY26 15% gearing target already slipped into FY27

Leverage remains elevated (30.3% reported gearing, interest cover down to 2.5x) with credit ratings at the lowest investment-grade notch (Baa3/BBB-), leaving limited room to absorb further shocks and no Corporation dividend currently being paid
Funds under management fell from $48.9b to $43.9b in FY26, directly eroding the recurring fee base that the 'Investments-led' strategy is supposed to be built around

Macro headwinds - rising Australian interest rates (57% floating-rate debt), elevated construction cost inflation through 2027, and a cyclical real estate market - directly pressure development feasibility, asset valuations and financing costs

Independent analysts (e.g. Morningstar) do not ascribe Lendlease an economic moat, viewing it as a capital-intensive participant in highly competitive development, funds management and construction markets against larger or more focused rivals (Charter Hall, Goodman Group, Mirvac, Dexus)
